title: Is Safer Better? The Impact of Guardrails on the Argumentative Strength of LLMs in Hate Speech Countering
findings: The paper's findings are general to counterspeech generation and are not broken down by the target of hate. Religion constitutes a significant portion (17.1%) of the targets in the hate speech dataset used. The main findings are that (1) the absence of safety guardrails can improve the cogency of counterspeech without compromising its perceived safety, and (2) attacking specific components of the hate speech argument, such as its implied statement or hateful premises, leads to higher-quality counterspeech. These findings apply to religious hate speech as it was part of the evaluation data.
